svg.title: Fig. 7 — A torus cut by a plane parallel to its axis
svg.desc: Redrawn from Robert C. Yates, A Handbook on Curves and Their Properties (1947), Fig. 7, page 9. Section: cassinian.

g.data-text: The axis of the torus (the arrow) and the cutting plane, parallel to the axis: its edges are the two long lines on the left.
The torus: the tube of circle radius ρ swept round the axis. Its outline in this view is the outer curve and the inner curve (the edge of the hole); the tube is shown cut open on the left.
Cross sections of the tube (circles of the generating circle): the front half in a full line, the half behind the tube dashed.

The distance a from the axis to the plane, the inner radius b of the generating circle, and the curve in which the plane cuts the torus (the arc on the left): a Cassinian curve; if b = a it is a lemniscate.
